# Step AA: saving in one module (TOOLS-308)

Lex (2026-11-15): pick 3 of the script editor review (TOOLS-296, report `script-editor-architecture-review-2026-11-15.html`, item 4 "Deepen the script-file module"): first tests for every way a script is saved, as it works today; then saving moves into one module with a small interface, and the same tests keep passing. Nothing on screen changes. Saving goes live only after Lex has clicked through it.

## What

1. **Characterization first.** `scripts/smoke-saving.mjs` drives the real editor in headless Chrome and checks every saving path as it works on `dev` before the move: a new script saved in the browser at once and named after its title, auto-save after about 1.5 s, Ctrl+S at once, a new script left untouched is not kept, reopening after a reload, the demo's draft with "Unsaved changes from …", Restore and Discard, Ctrl+S on the demo into the browser, a file from the computer auto-saved, "The file changed on disk at …" with "Save mine" and "Open that version", "Allow saving to …" and a refused Ctrl+S, Export → "Markdown file (.md)" moving a browser script to a file, the prompter link and Save to video folder carrying the saved script, switching scripts while a save runs (every save goes to the script it was made for), a failed write on a script the person left kept as unsaved changes, a B-roll link that stays with its own script when another script is saved under a new name during its link lookup, two tabs on one file, and Share to edit (the guest's words reach the host's file; the guest's browser keeps nothing).
2. **One module.** Saving moves out of `public/app.js` into `public/saving.js`. `createSaving({ script, editor, files, browser, drafts, clock, on })` gets the file system, local storage and the clock passed in (saving makes no network calls: the prompter link is made in the tab) and answers with `save`, `schedule`, `flush`, `stop`, `saveAs`, `saveMine`, `allow`, `open`, `queued` and `drafts`; what the person sees follows through `on`. Every save carries its own handle, name and text, so its write lands in the file it was made for even after another script opened, and its result changes the open script's record only while that script is still open. `save-queue.js` stays the module's pure queue. `saving.js` loads at startup with `app.js` (16 startup files instead of 15, about 4 KB more), as the code it holds did before. The browser's own file helpers (`writeHandle`, `permitted`) move along; `app.js` still hands them to the B-roll part.

## Where

`public/saving.js` (new), `public/app.js` (the save code is gone; it creates the module and calls it). Tests: `tests/saving.test.mjs` (the interface with a folder in memory, a clock the test moves and local storage in a Map: auto-save timing, saves that cross a script switch, a failed write on a left script kept as a draft, changed on disk and Save mine, Allow saving, saving into the browser and a switch meanwhile, Save as, drafts by name; and that `app.js` holds no save code). Browser check: `scripts/smoke-saving.mjs`.

## Browser check

`scripts/smoke-saving.mjs` on `wrangler dev` (it applies `_headers`) and headless Chrome, 1280 px, real typing and clicks; files on the computer are a folder in the browser's private file system that the stubbed pickers hand out. It passed on `dev` before the move (70 checks, twice) and passes unchanged after it; the page-hide check added after GPT's second look passes on both. The older suites (`smoke-csp`, `smoke-video-folder`, `smoke-broll-lazy`, `smoke-keep-all`, `smoke-room`, `smoke-relay`) pass on the same server. Evidence: `docs/agents/evidence/tools-308-browser.txt`.

## Done

Feature list: no change (saving moved into one module; nothing on screen changes)

### Proof

- Characterization tests for every saving path, passing on `dev` first: met. `node scripts/smoke-saving.mjs` on `origin/dev` 4e2bb84 printed 70 `ok` and `ok all`, twice (evidence, step 1).
- One saving module with the storage, clock and file system passed in; `app.js` only calls it: met. `tests/saving.test.mjs` failed first (`Cannot find module public/saving.js`), now 16 of 16 pass; its first test fails if `app.js` holds save code or the save queue again.
- The step-1 tests keep passing unchanged: met. The same `smoke-saving.mjs` after the move: 70 `ok`, `ok all`.
- A save always goes to the script it was made for: met. Browser: alpha.md's write held 900 ms, more typing, a switch to bravo.md and Ctrl+S there; alpha.md gets all of Alpha's words, bravo.md only Bravo's, and no write ever carried the other script's text. With a planted bug (a left script's snapshot written to the open script's file; diff and both runs in the evidence) both checks fail: the unit test, and in the browser `FAIL switch: no write ever went to the other script's file ([{"name":"bravo.md","text":"# Alpha …"}])`; with the code as it is both pass. Unit: the same with a held write in memory, and the open script's record follows only its own write. B-roll: with the demo's list loaded and the next script's link lookup held, a save under a new name gets no list (`B-roll link: the saved script does not take the demo's list`).
- Save as follows the script it was made for (GPT's second look, a real race, fixed): met. If another script was opened while Export → "Markdown file (.md)" was still writing, that other script took over the new file's place and name (its later typing would have saved into the moved script's file, and the moved script's B-roll link and draft went to it). `tests/saving.test.mjs` "another script opened while Save as writes…" failed first (the open script's record pointed at `moved.md`), now passes: the picked file gets the text and is listed, the open script keeps its own file, name, draft and B-roll keys, and the browser copy stays. A Ctrl+S on the open script made while that write ran then runs with its own flags (review round 2; its test failed on the round-1 code), and scripts the person left one after another meanwhile each get their own save, or a draft when the write is refused (second look in `kit pr`, P1; its test failed on the round-2 code).
- Page hide saves at once (GPT's gap): met. `runPageHide` passed on the code from before the move and passes now (evidence).
- Strict CSP green: met. `smoke-csp` 51 `ok`, `ok all`, no violation; `smoke-saving` checks for none on every page too.
- All unit and browser checks green: met. `kit specs` 464 pass; the six older browser suites pass.

### Declined

- Report bug (low, `app.js` Save as): a failed delete of the browser copy after "Markdown file (.md)" is still ignored, so that copy can stay in the switcher with the Browser tag. The only fix is to try the delete again later with no clear moment to do it, and the private file system refusing a delete of its own file is rare; left as it was so nothing changes in this move.
- Report bug (low, `video-folder.js`): saving again to the same video folder after shots were removed leaves their old pictures in `pictures/`. Fixing it means deleting files in a folder the person owns, which may hold pictures they put there; that is Lex's choice, asked through the lead.
- R2 nit (two ways to tell another script opened): `saveAs` uses the module's `opened` counter, `saveInBrowser` keeps the document check it had in `app.js` (the browser check characterizes it). One shared check would read better, but changing `saveInBrowser` changes when a demo saved during a Restore takes its new name; left as it was in this move.
- R2 nit ("Saving…" on the other script): while a Save as write that started on another script finishes, the open script shows "Saving…" for that moment; it was the same before the move and lasts one file write.
- GPT gap (Ctrl+S with neither browser saving nor a file picker): covered by the unit test "Ctrl+S where neither the browser nor a file picker can save downloads the script"; headless Chrome has both, so no browser check.

### Follow-ups

- Spec (P3): 4e3d531:docs/build/step-aa-saving-module.md:8 — P3 ticket: the step says `saving.js` adds "about 4 KB more" at startup. The evidence in `docs/agents/evidence/specs.txt` shows startup going from 463266 to 468623 bytes, which is 5357 bytes, or about 5 KB. The extra size probably came from the later Save as rounds. Fix: change the line to "about 5 KB more".
- Standards (P3): e837586:public/saving.js:222 — P3 race: after a Save as that finishes with another script open, `drain(true)` matches waiting saves by handle. A save asked for on a script with no file has no handle, so it can be run on the wrong script. Steps: on the demo, start Export → "Markdown file (.md)"; while the file is being written, press Ctrl+S (this waits in the queue with no handle); then open another script that also has no file (the demo again, or a file opened through the fallback file input). When the Save as finishes, `splitQueue(queue, null)` treats the demo's Ctrl+S as the new script's own save. `finish` then calls `save()`, and `saveInBrowser` saves the new script into the browser and renames it after its title, which the person never asked for. The demo's newer text from that Ctrl+S gets no draft either. It only happens during one file write, and with the older code this whole path broke the open script's record anyway, so this is a rare corner. Fix: when a request with no handle is left over after `opened` changed, don't let it become `current`. Either drop it from `queue.waiting` when `mine !== opened`, or keep it as a draft with `keepDraft(req.name, req.text)`.
- Standards (P3): 4e3d531:public/saving.js:247 — P3 race: `saveInBrowser` still empties the queue when it finishes, even if another script was opened while the browser copy was being made. This is the same pattern rounds 2 and 3 fixed in `saveAs`. Steps: Ctrl+S on the demo; while `browser.name` or `browser.create` is still running, switch to a file and press Ctrl+S. That click is dropped and comes back only as an auto-save 1.5 s later, which never shows the permission prompt. A script left in the same window doesn't get its waiting write either, though it keeps the draft that `persistDraft` stamped, so no words are lost. The older code behaved the same way and the window is only an OPFS create, so this is a nit. The Declined note about "two ways to tell another script opened" covers the doc check, but not this dropped queue. Fix: when `editor.doc() !== doc`, finish through `drain(true)` like `saveAs` does, or record the queue drop as a known difference in Declined.
- Validation gaps (gap): In `tests/saving.test.mjs`, nothing covers the moved script's own saves made during the Save as write. Test to add: start Save as on browser script `a.md` with the `moved.md` write held, change `ed.text` and call `save({ auto: true })` and then `flush()`, open `b.md`, then release. Assert that `a.md` (the browser copy that stays) holds the newer text, `moved.md` holds the text from when Save as started, and B's record is untouched.
- Validation gaps (gap): No test covers a Save as on the demo (no handle) where another script with no handle opens during the write after a queued Ctrl+S (the first Standards item). Test to add: `setup({ handle: null })`, `open(null, "# Demo\n")`, `pickSave` returns `moved.md` with the write held, call `save()` during the write, `open(null, "# Other\n")`, release. Assert that nothing goes to `from-title.md`, no `renamed` event fires, and `script.name` stays `demo.md`.
- Validation gaps (gap): No test covers `saveInBrowser` with another script opened and a Ctrl+S waiting on it (the second Standards item). Test to add: make `browser.create` wait on a gate, call `save()` on the demo, open `b.md`, change its text and call `save()`, release. Assert either that `b.md` is written with `asked === [true]`, or, if dropping it stays the chosen behaviour, that a single auto-save is scheduled. Either way the behaviour gets pinned down.
